title: Operator guide: heterogeneous model chain swap and rollback playbook
author: Daria Kozlov
content:
Summary

This playbook defines the operator-facing runbook for performing model swap (rollout) and rollback when private deployments host heterogeneous model chains: cascades, ensembles, fallback graphs, or hybrid quantization variants. It is intended for on-call operators, field engineers, and release engineers responsible for Private and Dedicated customer deployments (VPC and on-prem installations).

Scope

- Applies to model artifact swaps that change any of: model family, tokenizer, I/O schema, KV-cache format, quantization profile, or runtime kernel binding.
- Covers canary strategies, observability checks, automated gating, manual rollback criteria, and post-rollback validation.
- Does NOT cover host-level OS upgrades, network reconfiguration, or hardware replacements (see separate runbooks).

Audience

- Operator (first-responder)
- Field site engineer
- Release engineer

Prerequisites and Safety Gates

1) Owner approvals and scheduled maintenance window noted in ticketing system.
2) Artifact compatibility matrix entry exists for the target model(s) and is approved by Model Onboarding.
3) Snapshot of runtime state and KV-cache exported (if applicable). Command: 

  rdinv export-kv-cache --tenant $TENANT --model $MODEL --out /tmp/kv-$MODEL-$(date -I).tar.gz

4) Canary cluster or shadow traffic configured (minimum 5% traffic or 10 QPS, whichever is larger).
5) Rollback escrow prepared: operator credentials, artifact versions to restore, and precomputed migration plan.

Terminology

- Heterogeneous model chain: a runtime configuration where inference flows through multiple model artifacts (e.g., classifier -> policy -> reranker), or multiple model variants are used depending on routing rules.
- Model swap: replacing one or more artifacts in the chain with a new version or variant.
- KV-cache (session/state) compatibility: whether cached token/key-value tensors are interoperable across model versions.

High-level approach

1) Verify compatibility and preflight checks.
2) Deploy to canary/validation tenant(s) with isolated traffic.
3) Run synthetic and real traffic validation (quality + latency + error budget).
4) Gradually increase rollout (20% -> 50% -> 100%) with checkpoints.
5) If thresholds breach, execute rollback with a documented order-of-operations to preserve state.

Preflight verification checklist (operator)

- [ ] Artifact manifest signed and verified (sha256, provenance).
- [ ] Model onboarding compatibility matrix ID present and status = APPROVED.
- [ ] Tokenizer schema delta validated (tokenization diffs within allowed tolerance).
- [ ] KV-cache migration script (if required) present and dry-run tested.
- [ ] Canary route and sampling configured in routing policy.
- [ ] Observability dashboards open and baseline metrics recorded.
- [ ] Rollback artifacts deposited in escrow and accessible by operator.

Canary and validation phase

1) Deploy to a single canary tenant. Use progressive traffic shaping. Example rollout policy snippet (YAML):

  rollout_policy:
    strategy: progressive
    steps:
      - percent: 5
        duration: 30m
      - percent: 20
        duration: 1h
      - percent: 50
        duration: 2h

2) Run validation suites:
  - Synthetic prompts (prompt set ID: hetero-chain-smoke-v2)
  - End-to-end latency SLO tests (p50/p95/p99 checkpoints)
  - Error rate (5xx, 4xx) and exception traces monitoring
  - Quality regressions: BLEU/ROUGE/semantic similarity or evaluator hooks configured in Redwood Optimize

Primary success thresholds (canary):

- Latency: p95 <= baseline p95 + 25ms
- Error rate: increase <= 0.1 percentage points absolute
- Quality: no regression above tolerance for critical prompt set (tolerance defined in onboarding matrix)

Progressive rollout and gating

- If all canary thresholds pass, advance to 20% for 1 hour. Monitor the same metrics plus resource utilization (GPU memory, kernel stalls).
- Operator must check model-serving runtime logs for mismatched KV-cache warnings or deserialization errors.
- At each gate, record a signed release note in the ticket and capture key metrics snapshot.

Rollback criteria (any gate)

- Latency p95 > baseline p95 + 50ms for two consecutive monitoring windows (5m windows).
- Error rate delta > 0.5 percentage points absolute.
- Quality regression above allowed threshold for critical prompt set.
- Unrecoverable runtime errors: kernel OOMs, disk-full on snapshot path, KV-cache corruption diagnostics.

Rollback runbook (order-of-operations)

1) Immediately pause rollout and mark operator command in ticket.
2) Scale down new model variant routing to 0% using control plane API. Example API call:

  redwoodctl routing set --route $ROUTE --percent 0 --model $PREVIOUS_MODEL_V

3) If KV-cache migration ran and is irreversible, follow forensic snapshot procedure:
  - Quarantine affected tenants: redirect traffic to safe fallback model variant or sandbox.
  - Restore KV snapshot: rdinv restore-kv-cache --tenant $TENANT --from /escrow/kv-$MODEL-backup.tar.gz

4) Revert any config changes to autoscaling or node pools made for the swap.

5) Validate post-rollback health: run smoke prompts and check p50/p95, error rates, and model output sanity.

6) Open incident record if rollback due to service degradation; attach artifacts and logs for triage.

Operator checklist for long-tail state recovery

- Confirm KV-cache is consistent across all nodes (hash checks).
- Check for orphaned ephemeral sessions and expunge if older than configured TTL (default 24h).
- If partial state drift observed, coordinate with Model Onboarding for state reconciliation or replay.

Special cases: ensemble and cascade chains

- Ensemble swaps: treat each ensemble member as an independent rollout artifact with its own gates. Only advance global rollout when majority of members pass their canaries.
- Cascade chains: deploy downstream model placeholders before upstream swap to avoid input schema mismatch. Use a compatibility shim when necessary to normalize intermediate outputs.

Observability and critical signals

Open dashboards and alerts (examples):

- Model latency by route (p50/p95/p99)
- 5xx/4xx error rate by model and tenant
- Kernel OOM/ CUDA memory alarms
- KV-cache deserialization error count
- Semantic quality evaluator score (rolling window)

Important log snippets to watch for (grep patterns):

- "kv_cache: deserialization_error"
- "tokenizer: unknown_token_warning"
- "kernel_bind: fallback_to_cpu"

Commands and quick references

- Pause rollout:
  redwoodctl rollout pause --id $ROLLOUT_ID
- Set route percent:
  redwoodctl routing set --route $ROUTE --percent $N --model $MODEL_V
- Export kv cache snapshot:
  rdinv export-kv-cache --tenant $TENANT --model $MODEL --out $PATH
- Restore kv cache snapshot:
  rdinv restore-kv-cache --tenant $TENANT --from $PATH

Post-incident actions and evidence capture

- Preserve logs for 30 days in incident evidence bucket: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/$INCIDENT_ID
- Capture runtime heap/metrics snapshot and store with incident tag.
- Convene triage with Model Onboarding and Runtime team within 48 hours.

Compatibility table (operator quick lookup)

This is an illustrative table; real compatibility entries live in Model Onboarding. Columns: Model family | Tokenizer compatible | KV-cache compatible | Recommended migration step

- family-a-v* | yes | no | preflight conversion script required (see migration-helpers/conv-v1-to-v2)
- family-b-quant | same | same | safe forward/backward KV-cache; no migration
- family-c-cascade | different | no | deploy shim: cascade-normalizer v0.3

Appendix: example small incident timeline (operator)

- T+00:00 Deploy to canary (5%). Baseline snapshots captured.
- T+00:30 Canary reported p95 +120ms -> operator paused rollout.
- T+00:34 Operator reduced routing to 0% and initiated KV snapshot restore.
- T+01:10 Post-rollback validation passed for smoke prompts.
- T+02:00 Incident opened and triage scheduled.

Ownership and escalation

- Primary: eng-private-deployments (oncall)
- Secondary: eng-serving-runtime (kernel/ops)
- Tertiary: applied-ml-and-evals / Model Onboarding (compatibility and quality)
